config.title: filter and backdrop-filter

intro.title: filter and backdrop-filter
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a visually engaging webpage that demonstrates how to apply special visual effects to images and backgrounds. You will learn the core concepts of the CSS `filter` and `backdrop-filter` properties, which allow you to modify elements with effects like blur, brightness, and contrast. The main technologies involved are CSS properties and values, which you will apply directly in a CSS file. By the end, you'll be able to create dynamic, polished visual designs using these powerful styling tools.
intro.usecase: The filter and backdrop-filter properties are essential for creating modern, visually engaging interfaces that users encounter daily. In photo editing applications like Instagram or Photoshop, filters apply effects like blur, brightness, and saturation adjustments to images. Backdrop-filter is commonly used in modal dialogs, notification panels, and iOS-style control centers to create frosted glass effects that blur the background content while keeping foreground elements readable. Developers implement these properties in dashboards, admin panels, and media-rich websites to enhance visual hierarchy, focus user attention, and create immersive experiences without heavy image processing.

objectives: Apply filter properties to modify image appearance with blur, brightness, and contrast effects
Configure backdrop-filter to create frosted glass effects on overlay elements
Construct a photo gallery interface with interactive filter controls
Manipulate filter values dynamically using CSS custom properties
Integrate multiple filter functions to achieve complex visual transformations
Implement responsive filter adjustments for different screen sizes
Control filter intensity through precise numerical values and percentages

steps.title: Set up the HTML structure for filter examples
steps.instruction: Create a container div with three child div elements inside it. Give the container a class of 'filter-container' and each child div a class of 'filter-box'.
steps.hint: You'll need to write HTML structure with a parent div containing three child divs. Use the class names provided.
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic HTML structure with a container and three child elements that we can apply CSS filters to in later steps.
successCriteria: The code contains a div with class 'filter-container' that has three child div elements, each with class 'filter-box'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three child div elements inside the container, and that all elements have the correct class names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what we need. Remember to create one container div with three child divs, using the specified class names.

steps.title: Apply the blur() filter to the first element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that applies a blur filter to the first child div. Use the selector `.filter-example:nth-child(1)` and set `filter: blur(2px);`.
steps.hint: The nth-child(1) selector targets the first element with the class filter-example. The blur() function creates a softening effect.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first colored box will appear slightly blurred, demonstrating the visual effect of the blur() filter function.
successCriteria: The CSS rule for the first filter-example element includes filter: blur(2px);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct selector and the exact filter property with blur(2px).
steps.feedbackWrong: The blur filter wasn't applied correctly. Check that you're targeting the first element with .filter-example:nth-child(1) and using filter: blur(2px);

steps.title: Apply the grayscale() filter to the second element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the second child div to apply a grayscale filter at 100% intensity.
steps.hint: Use the selector .filter-example:nth-child(2) and set filter: grayscale(100%).
steps.expectedOutcome: The second element will appear completely black and white.
successCriteria: The selector .filter-example:nth-child(2) has filter: grayscale(100%) applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're targeting the second element with the correct selector and using filter: grayscale(100%).
steps.feedbackWrong: The second element doesn't have the grayscale filter applied. Check your selector and CSS property.

steps.title: Apply multiple filters to the third element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the third child element that applies both sepia(50%) and brightness(120%) filters together.
steps.hint: Use the filter property with multiple functions separated by spaces. Target the third child using :nth-child(3).
steps.expectedOutcome: The third element will have a sepia tint and increased brightness applied simultaneously.
successCriteria: The CSS rule for .filter-example:nth-child(3) includes filter: sepia(50%) brightness(120%);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're targeting the third child and using both filter functions separated by spaces.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to create a rule for the third element with both sepia and brightness filters.

steps.title: Create a backdrop-filter example structure
steps.instruction: Add a new section with a background image div and a semi-transparent overlay div to your HTML structure.
steps.hint: You'll need to create a new container section with two nested divs - one for the background and one for the overlay that will use backdrop-filter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new HTML section with two nested div elements is added to prepare for backdrop-filter demonstration.
successCriteria: The HTML structure contains a new section with a background div and an overlay div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Style the backdrop-filter container elements
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the backdrop-filter container and overlay elements with appropriate dimensions, positioning, and background properties.
steps.hint: You'll need to create two new CSS selectors: one for the container and one for the overlay. Set width, height, position, and background properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The backdrop-filter container and overlay elements will have proper dimensions, positioning, and background styling ready for backdrop-filter effects.
successCriteria: CSS rules for .backdrop-container and .backdrop-overlay are added with width, height, position, and background properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Apply backdrop-filter blur to the overlay
steps.instruction: Add the CSS rule `backdrop-filter: blur(5px);` to the overlay element in your backdrop-filter example.
steps.hint: Look for the element that should have the blur effect applied to its background. Use the backdrop-filter property with the blur() function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The overlay element will have a blurred background effect applied to it.
successCriteria: The CSS rule includes `backdrop-filter: blur(5px);` applied to the correct overlay element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the correct property (`backdrop-filter`) and function (`blur(5px)`).
steps.feedbackWrong: The backdrop-filter blur wasn't applied correctly. Check that you're using the right property and value syntax.

steps.title: Enhance backdrop-filter with multiple effects
steps.instruction: Update the backdrop-filter property in the overlay to include both blur(5px) and brightness(70%) effects.
steps.hint: You can chain multiple backdrop-filter functions by separating them with a space. Add brightness(70%) after the existing blur(5px).
steps.expectedOutcome: The overlay will have a blurred background with reduced brightness, creating a more dramatic backdrop effect.
successCriteria: The backdrop-filter property includes both blur(5px) and brightness(70%) functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both blur(5px) and brightness(70%) to the backdrop-filter property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The backdrop-filter property doesn't contain the required effects. Update it to include blur(5px) brightness(70%).

steps.title: Add hover effects to demonstrate interactivity
steps.instruction: Add a :hover pseudo-class to the first filter example (.filter-example:nth-child(1)) to increase its blur value from the current amount to 8px.
steps.hint: Use the :hover selector after the existing rule to change the filter property when the user hovers over the element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first filter example will have an interactive hover effect that increases the blur intensity.
successCriteria: A :hover rule for .filter-example:nth-child(1) is added with filter: blur(8px);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a hover rule, but check if the blur value is set to 8px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect is missing or incorrect. Add :hover for .filter-example:nth-child(1) with filter: blur(8px);
